elaine_cs: Zero2One onboarding hiccup. Their e2e shows a burst of 200s then a cluster of 429s right when the ephemeral token swap happens. They9re on browser-sdk v0.9.2 behind a custom proxy. Any quick triage tips? :thinking:

raj_sdk: Sounds like multiple tabs/requests racing at refresh. Do they use our client preflight or a custom preflight flow? If the proxy replays requests on retry it amplifies the stampede.

elaine_cs: Customer says: 
```
token rotate at 18:03:12 UTC, new token fetched
parallel init 8 sockets, one per service
then ~30s window of 429s across endpoints
```
They also mentioned their proxy occasionally resets keepalives.

sam_eng: Proxy resets + concurrent init = double whammy. Two short repros: 1) disable parallel warming (set `maxParallelInit: 2`), 2) add small randomized jitter on token refresh (100-600ms). If proxy is replaying, we9ll still see correlated IP-level bursts.

marta_se: I suggested they run a quick dev repro with `MAX_TABS=3` and a small script to simulate token rotates. Also asked them to capture our `x-request-id` and `x-ratewindow` from ingress headers.

elaine_cs: I sent them a one-line snippet to add to the SDK init: 
```
Redwood.init({ maxParallelInit: 2, tokenRefreshSplayMs: 300 });
```
Also asked them to toggle proxy keepalive to off briefly to confirm the proxy is contributing.

raj_sdk: If they can't change client, we can offer a temporary account config: bump ephemeral TTL from 60->120s for 48h and enable soft-shed smoothing on their API key. Ops will need sign-off. Pros/cons: reduces refresh rate but increases window for leaked tokens.

marta_se: They9d prefer a platform tweak for speed. I can draft the risk/rollback steps: record affected API key, add TTL flag, monitor for token reuse or unexpected long-lived tokens, revert after 48h.

sam_eng: For diagnostics in the playbook, include commands to grep ingress logs: 
```
grep "x-request-id" /var/log/redwood/ingress.log | grep <api_key>
awk '/x-ratewindow/ {print $0}' | grep <ip_or_key>
```
Capture if burst IPs are identical. If multiple IPs, client-side changes required.

elaine_cs: I'll attach the playbook to case Z2O-1287 and ask for the customer's consent to the TTL bump + smoothing. If they approve, schedule change for low-traffic window and monitor dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example/account/zero2one/metrics

onboard-bot: Note added to Z2O-1287 by elaine_cs 18:41 UTC14  "prepared TTL bump + smoothing playbook; awaiting customer ok"

raj_sdk: One more: check whether their proxy adds an extra `Authorization` header during retries; double-headers can cause our preflight to be treated as distinct keys and evade client-side backoff. If we see that, loop in infra to confirm header normalization.

elaine_cs: Great. Will follow up after their test. Thanks everyone. :pray:
